internal_decisions: merge sorts a copy by (start, end), so the input list is untouched

checks.detail: test_shifts (AC-004..006) pass; only test_rules and test_schedule error, because WP-03 and WP-04 modules don't exist yet

internal_decisions: Used re.fullmatch so trailing newlines are rejected
Tests import Interval from roster.intervals (WP-01 already in repo)
Person names are stripped in shifts() and minutes() lookups too, so they match what assign() stored.
Touching shifts on the same day are allowed, because overlaps() treats them as not overlapping.
Rest = day difference*1440 + next.start - prev.end; violation when strictly less than min_rest (exact rest allowed).

plan: Contracts: Interval bounds, merge/gaps edges, Schedule->rest_violations with overnight shifts, tested from the consumer side (qa/test_qa.py).
Edge cases: failed assign changes nothing, name stripping, handover touching, trailing newline, shifts() returns a copy, input list not mutated. All pass.
Defects: D1 and D2 are low severity and their tests stay red on purpose.
Discarded: non-functional (not in architecture) and regression (no pre-existing behaviour beyond the version test).

defects.repro: parse_shift('0٩:00-17:00') (Arabic-Indic digit nine) returns Interval(540, 1020) instead of raising ValueError. Python's \d matches any Unicode decimal digit. Test: qa/test_qa.py::test_d1_unicode_digits_rejected
defects.fix: Use [0-9] in the regex, or compile it with re.ASCII.
defects.if_skipped: Non-ASCII digit text is accepted as valid shift text. The contract allows only HH:MM digits, so the effect is minor.

defects.repro: Interval(1.5, 10) is accepted. The contract says start and end are ints. Test: qa/test_qa.py::test_d2_non_int_interval_rejected
defects.fix: In __post_init__, raise ValueError if either field is not an int (excluding bool).
defects.if_skipped: Float or bool bounds get through and can give non-integer minutes later.

gaps: The hook blocked one bash call that used inline python. I did not try to get around it and used the Write tool instead.
Whether coverage_gaps and conflict detection should count an overnight shift's spill into the next day is unspecified in the architecture, so I did not test it.

advisory.problem: AC-011 has a single scenario and no positive cross-day violation. A rule that only compares same-day neighbours, or one that returns a constant, still passes. Overnight shifts (end > 1440) are not exercised.
advisory.evidence: def rest_violations(s, m): return [(a[0], b[0]) for a, b in zip(s, s[1:]) if a[0] == b[0] and b[1].start - a[1].end < m] passes. So does a constant [(D5, D5)] when the list is non-empty.

advisory.problem: gaps is tested with one sorted case. It does not test intervals that extend beyond the window, an empty list, or unsorted or overlapping input. merge is not tested with touching or nested intervals.
advisory.evidence: A gaps that assumes sorted input and no clipping passes. A merge that uses `<` instead of `<=` for touching intervals also passes.

advisory.problem: The conflict boundary is not tested: touching shifts for the same person on the same day, or an overlap of the same hours on a different day. The coverage_gaps test does not check that overnight shifts are excluded or included.
advisory.evidence: An assign that raises ConflictError when end >= existing.start (touching counts as a conflict) still passes.

advisory.problem: overlaps is checked only for partial overlap, a disjoint pair and touching. It is not checked for containment or for the symmetric argument order.
advisory.evidence: overlaps = a.start < b.start < a.end or b.start < a.start < b.end gives True for both AC-001 cases and False for the touching case. It gives False for the nested pair Interval(0,100) and Interval(10,20), which is wrong.
